summary: Output-only gated-delta verification, atomic accepted-prefix recurrent recovery and a CUDA device commit reference
implementation_scope: Bounded C++20 FP64 host gated-delta chain, physical accepted-node mapping, after-token checkpoints and private sibling commit; Python formula; generic FP32 CUDA reference verify with per-column checkpoints, recompute or deferred replay and device-count accepted-state selection. Model projections, casts and tuned kernels remain external; a pure-Python two-pass chunked prefill (chunk-parallel triangular solve, then a sequential matrix-product pass) checked against the token-by-token recurrence

agent_guidance.use_when: A short speculative accepted prefix can be reconstructed more cheaply than retaining a full recurrent matrix after every proposed token
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Recovery work outweighs state-storage savings, recurrence/cast semantics differ, or complete continuation state cannot be restored
provides: Finite bounded gated-delta arithmetic and output-only chain verification
Recovery from retained initial state and per-node inputs without per-token matrix snapshots
Absolute after-token checkpoint semantics and accepted ordinal to physical-node mapping
Single-use atomic partial/zero commit, private sibling hook, cancellation and standalone native example

Generic FP32 CUDA reference verify and device-side accepted-state commit by per-column checkpoints, recompute from saved inputs, or deferred replay at the next verify, selected from a device-held accepted count
Two-pass chunked prefill: state-independent T, W, Ub and decayed q.k per chunk in parallel, then a sequential pass of matrix products only
engine_supplies: Model projections, gates, head mappings, activation/state cast rules and sampler acceptance
All convolution, index, target/draft and other continuation siblings
Native kernels, source/destination reservations, producer ordering and failure settlement
Materialization of correction or bonus tokens and full-model qualification
preserve: State at boundary B is after B materialized tokens
Select checkpoint accepted ordinal B minus initial count minus one through the physical-node map
Recover the declared ordinary recurrence and every required sibling
Withhold publication and preserve committed state on any failure

On the device, select the accepted state from the device-held count without a host read; keep commit rerunnable with a smaller count (a separate round-start state, or a deferred count applied at the next verify)
adapt: Head batching, tensor layout, supported shapes, representations and recurrence kernels
Owned graph staging and side-stream recovery with explicit readiness joins
Device strategy: per-column checkpoints (memory), recompute from the start state (repeated steps) or deferred replay (no start copy, scalar commit)

code_files.purpose: Bounded native host recurrence and atomic private recovery; after-token checkpoint mapping from Core (crit::core::checkpoint_node)
Immutable FP64 formula and chain recovery worked example
Standalone native nonsequential-path and partial-checkpoint POC
Native example and independent recurrent regression build against Core (installed SDK or this checkout)
FP32 CUDA reference interface for multi-head verify and checkpoint, recompute or deferred commit from a device accepted count
Reference one-block-per-head, one-thread-per-value-column gated-delta kernels, not for performance
Two-pass chunked gated-delta prefill and the token-by-token recurrence for comparison

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ standard library for formula; CMake 3.28+, C++20 and Core (crit::core) for native host POC; CUDA C++20 with Core CRIT_CORE_CUDA for the device reference
requires.model: Declared gated-delta recurrence with caller-supplied projected/gated step inputs and complete sibling restoration
requires.workload: One rooted verification chain per round; bounded physical nodes, outputs, state, siblings and positions

contract.input: Explicit geometry/limits, owned FP64 starting matrix at an absolute after-token count, topologically numbered nodes and a selected physical path
contract.output: Provisional verification outputs, then a complete accepted snapshot and optional exact boundary checkpoint; on the device, outputs plus a live state selected from the accepted count
contract.ownership: The loop owns input copies and private snapshots; sibling callbacks touch private bytes and settle all work; accesses are serialized. Device kernels borrow caller-owned start, live, checkpoint, work and step buffers on the caller stream
contract.failure: Reject invalid gates/layouts/paths/bounds and numerical overflow; failed/cancelled commit consumes its round while preserving committed state
contract.core_boundary: After-token checkpoint selection is Core's checkpoint_node, and slot bookkeeping (live, round-start, per-column or recompute scratch, in-place) is Core's StateCache with RecurrentCommit column_checkpoints, recompute or in_place; this entry keeps the recurrence arithmetic, the private recovery transaction and the device kernels. Use Core resource/readiness/publication/lifetime contracts without model-specific Core semantics

dependencies: CMake 3.28+, C++20 standard library and Core's state header (crit::core)
CUDA runtime for the device reference

validation.host: Independent long-double matrix-transition oracle, all accepted lengths, absolute boundary/tree mapping, varied chunk decomposition and boundary-adjacent continuation, zero-step rounds after acceptance, exact sibling frontiers, private sibling failures, zero/partial/cancelled/stale commits and finite limits; two-pass chunked prefill equals the token-by-token recurrence for several chunk sizes, normalizations and partial last chunks
validation.native: C++20 host example and regressions; CUDA reference against the FP64 host oracle over 96 geometries for outputs and every accepted count within 2e-5 + 2e-5*|ref|, with bitwise agreement of checkpoint and recompute commits, and 96 multi-round deferred commits (including truncation reruns) bitwise equal to checkpoint commits, with the pending count consumed once across flushes and abandoned rounds. Engine casts, asynchronous ordering and model continuation remain unqualified
validation.performance: Unmeasured; retained state is bounded independently of speculative matrix snapshot count
